common.classification: retained Endpoint Transit acquisition decoder closure
common.rationale: #117 removes the old Node receiving issuer. These exact decoder, verifier, and client-message dependencies remain direct consumers of the explicitly out-of-scope Endpoint acquisition and fixed-Grant verification closures already registered in this allowlist; none can sign, initialize, open, or serve an issuer root.

common.retirement: Repeat exact consumer and persisted-wire analysis in a separate bounded Route/transit compatibility audit after the retained User-route and Endpoint consumers receive their own disposition.

common.classification: unwired shared legacy Route, Entry, credential, reachability, and Service leaves
common.rationale: These shared-owner leaves were reachable only through the retired v1 participant graph. #157 preserves them because their packages and protocols have broader historical evidence and their deletion is outside the exclusive process-composition boundary.
common.retirement: Create a bounded shared-owner retirement card from the post-#112 caller audit, name each remaining production/test consumer, and delete or reclassify these exact leaves without treating #112 as authority to remove shared Service Connection or Route behavior.

windows-amd64.rationale: Removing the old cross-platform Rendezvous listener additionally makes these exact shared framing leaves unreachable in Windows production. Linux production still reaches them through retained Route consumers, and issue #120 does not authorize deleting shared Route grammar.
windows-amd64.retirement: Remove this Windows allowance if a maintained Windows Route consumer is selected, or when a separate bounded consumer audit retires or assigns narrower platform ownership to this shared framing closure.

windows-amd64.classification: Windows projection of retained Endpoint Transit Grant verification

windows-amd64.retirement: Remove with the retained Endpoint Transit acquisition and fixed-Grant verification closure after its dedicated post-#112 consumer disposition.

windows-amd64.classification: selected Linux-only protected text runtime closure

windows-amd64.retirement: Remove this Windows allowance if a maintained Windows protected runtime is selected, or when the Linux-only runtime and its shared closure are retired or assigned narrower platform build ownership.
